declined_new_candidates.reason: Two colored light footprints would compete with the repeated local pigment comparison; neutral daylight better serves this scene.
Red versus navy/violet illumination is a different expressive relation and would reduce this arm material-owner comparison.
A global green bias does not deepen the violet/ochre pigment and reflective-trim hierarchy.

vo_pa_bounded_metal_trim_1.evidence: Native and 512px whole-frame views show a narrow warm-gold gunwale and railing perimeter on the boat, separate from the much larger violet hull and matte violet apron. Gold remains a bounded trim owner rather than a flat gold body field or frame-wide illumination.

scale_evidence.thumbnail: The fine gold upper outline remains distinct from the broad violet hull and apron at 512px.
scale_evidence.native: Gunwale segments, upright posts and rail bends show small local gold reflections and darker intervening metal segments.

vo_pa_bounded_metal_trim_2.evidence: At native scale the brighter glints follow individual metal rail and post directions; darker segments stay within the same narrow trim. At thumbnail scale the bounded warm perimeter remains reflective and separate while the neighboring apron is diffusely shaded violet, with no gold wash across it.

scale_evidence.thumbnail: Bright warm rail segments trace the boat edge while the broad adjacent apron remains matte purple.
scale_evidence.native: Narrow rail/post highlights vary along the curved perimeter, and apron fibers/folds retain soft diffuse purple shading.

attribution_limit: Traceability from source, selection, literal prompt and exact audited runtime to a satisfying image is verified. The initial image already had incidental gold trim, so isolated causal improvement is not established.
